notes: extracted_rule_ids = rule_id in *_risk_categories.json (refined); extracted_raw_rule_ids = rule_id in *_all_extracted_rules.json. origin: extracted | modified | added | interpretation (a reading the wiki does not force) | tool_spec (taken from the τ-bench tool description). verification_types: data needed: state (current args + latest DB objects in tool outputs), tool_log (earlier tool calls/results), structural (format of the current agent turn), dialogue (message content; LLM judge).

rules.description: The agent must list the action details to the user before calling any tool that updates the booking database (booking, cancelling, changing flights or cabin, editing baggage, or updating passengers).
rules.wiki_quote: Before taking any actions that update the booking database (booking, modifying flights, editing baggage, upgrading cabin class, or updating passenger information), you must list the action details
rules.notes: Split from compound R1, which also used the wrong subject. AMBIGUITY: the wiki's parenthetical list omits cancellation, but cancel_reservation updates the booking database, so it is included under the literal head phrase 'any actions that update the booking database'. send_certificate writes to the user profile, not the booking database, and is excluded. Review this. Decision (Step 1 close-out): cancel_reservation stays in scope and send_certificate stays excluded. The cancellation part of the scope is an INTERPRETATION, kept explicit so it can be ablated later.

rules.description: The agent must obtain an explicit 'yes' from the user, given after the action details were listed, before calling any tool that updates the booking database.
rules.wiki_quote: obtain explicit user confirmation (yes) to proceed.
rules.notes: Same tool scope and ambiguity as AIR-R001. Decision (Step 1 close-out): same scope as AIR-R001. The cancellation part is an INTERPRETATION (ablation candidate).

rules.description: The agent must not provide information, knowledge, or procedures that were not provided by the user or by the available tools.
rules.wiki_quote: You should not provide any information, knowledge, or procedures not provided by the user or available tools
rules.notes: Fixes R9 (inverted subject, 'TauBench' substituted for 'the user', invented 'do not request'). Facts in the wiki (refund timing, certificate remainder) are policy knowledge the agent may state.

rules.description: The agent must not give subjective recommendations or comments.
rules.wiki_quote: or give subjective recommendations or comments.
rules.notes: Dropped by the extraction at the raw-rule stage.

rules.description: The agent must make at most one tool call per turn.
rules.wiki_quote: You should only make one tool call at a time
rules.notes: R47 had the user as subject. Verification type changed to structural: a property of the current model turn (number of tool calls), not of history.

rules.description: The agent must not respond to the user and make a tool call in the same turn.
rules.wiki_quote: if you make a tool call, you should not respond to the user simultaneously. … If you respond to the user, you should not make a tool call at the same time.
rules.notes: One rule for both directions of the same constraint. The τ-bench runtime may already enforce this structurally, depending on the agent loop. Verification type changed to structural: a property of the current model turn (text alongside a tool call).

rules.description: The agent must deny (refuse to carry out) user requests that are against this policy.
rules.wiki_quote: You should deny user requests that are against this policy.
rules.notes: Meta-rule. The shield enforces it at action level by blocking any action that violates another rule. At message level, the agent must state a refusal rather than pretend compliance.

rules.description: The agent must not transfer the user to a human agent unless the request cannot be handled within the scope of the agent's actions or the user explicitly asks for a human agent.
rules.wiki_quote: You should transfer the user to a human agent if and only if the request cannot be handled within the scope of your actions. … As an airline agent, you can help users book, modify, or cancel flight reservations.
rules.notes: Restores the 'only if' half of 'if and only if'. NOTE: the τ-bench tool description also allows a transfer when the user explicitly asks for a human. The wiki does not, so the literal wiki reading is kept. AIR-R044 is an explicit case where a transfer is required. Decision (Step 1 close-out): the second disjunct ('the user explicitly asks for a human agent') comes from the τ-bench transfer_to_human_agents tool description, not the wiki; hence origin tool_spec. Precedence: AIR-R007 (deny requests against policy) and AIR-R036 (never transfer a passenger-count change) override the explicit-request permission. An explicit request for a human does not justify a transfer of a request the policy says to deny, nor of a passenger-count change.

rules.description: The agent must transfer the user to a human agent when the request cannot be handled within the scope of the agent's actions.
rules.wiki_quote: You should transfer the user to a human agent if and only if the request cannot be handled within the scope of your actions. … As an airline agent, you can help users book, modify, or cancel flight reservations.
rules.notes: Precedence: requests that are within scope but against policy are denied (AIR-R007), not transferred. Requests to change the passenger count are never transferred (AIR-R036). Decision (Step 1 close-out): unchanged obligation. An explicit request for a human only PERMITS a transfer (AIR-R008); it does not oblige one. Precedence as in AIR-R008: AIR-R007 and AIR-R036 take priority.

rules.description: The agent must not book a flight, or add a new flight to an existing reservation, unless the flight's status on that date is 'available'.
rules.wiki_quote: If the status is "delayed" or "on time", the flight has not taken off, cannot be booked. … If the status is "flying", the flight has taken off but not landed, cannot be booked.
rules.notes: The whole Domain Basic section was dropped by the extraction. AMBIGUITY: τ-bench data also contains flight-date statuses 'landed' and 'cancelled', which the wiki never mentions, and the API books only 'available'. The literal list is kept here. A stricter 'only available' reading is an open question. For update_reservation_flights the rule applies to newly added segments only; this is an interpretation. Decision (Step 1 close-out): stricter 'only available' reading adopted (an interpretation). The wiki lists only 'delayed', 'on time' and 'flying' as non-bookable; τ-bench data also has 'landed' and 'cancelled'. The τ-bench API books only 'available' (book_reservation.py:65, update_reservation_flights.py:49).

rules.description: When booking a flight, the agent must obtain the user id first, before collecting the trip type, origin, and destination.
rules.wiki_quote: The agent must first obtain the user id
rules.notes: Split from R2 and given the agent as subject.

rules.description: The agent must ask the user for the trip type, origin, and destination before booking a flight.
rules.wiki_quote: then ask for the trip type, origin, destination.
rules.notes: R2 imposed an order 'trip type, then origin, then destination' that the wiki does not state. The wiki lists the three items unordered.

rules.description: The agent must not book a reservation with more than five passengers.
rules.wiki_quote: Passengers: Each reservation can have at most five passengers.

rules.description: The agent must collect the first name, last name, and date of birth of every passenger before booking.
rules.wiki_quote: The agent needs to collect the first name, last name, and date of birth for each passenger.
rules.notes: Deterministic part: every passenger in the call has all three fields. Checking that the values come from the user, not fabricated, falls under AIR-R003.

rules.description: The agent must book all passengers of a reservation on the same flights in the same cabin.
rules.wiki_quote: All passengers must fly the same flights in the same cabin.
rules.notes: The book_reservation schema already guarantees this: one cabin and one flight list per reservation. Kept for completeness.

rules.description: The agent must not use more than one travel certificate as payment for a reservation.
rules.wiki_quote: Payment: each reservation can use at most one travel certificate
rules.notes: Count payment_ids with the 'certificate_' prefix.

rules.description: The agent must not use more than one credit card as payment for a reservation.
rules.wiki_quote: at most one credit card

rules.description: The agent must not use more than three gift cards as payment for a reservation.
rules.wiki_quote: and at most three gift cards.

rules.description: The agent must only use payment methods that already exist in the user's profile when booking.
rules.wiki_quote: All payment methods must already be in user profile for safety reasons.
rules.notes: The clause sits under 'Book flight'. The τ-bench API also rejects unknown payment ids on the update tools.

rules.description: When the booking user is a regular member, the agent must set nonfree_baggages to exactly the number of checked bags in excess of the pooled free allowance (number of passengers x per-passenger allowance), with a per-passenger allowance of 0 bags in basic economy, 1 in economy and 2 in business.
rules.wiki_quote: If the booking user is a regular member, 0 free checked bag for each basic economy passenger, 1 free checked bag for each economy passenger, and 2 free checked bags for each business passenger.
rules.notes: Restores 'booking user': the tier is the reservation owner's, not the passengers'. Check: nonfree_baggages == max(0, total_baggages - allowance x passengers). The table appears under 'Book flight'. Applying it to later bag additions is an interpretation. Decision (Step 1 close-out): exact equality (charging for a free bag is also wrong). The allowance is POOLED across passengers (an interpretation; the wiki gives a per-passenger allowance). Checked against the tool source: total_baggages and nonfree_baggages are reservation-level totals in book_reservation (book_reservation.py:48-49, priced at line 77) and update_reservation_baggages (update_reservation_baggages.py:22, 34-35).

rules.description: When the booking user is a silver member, the agent must set nonfree_baggages to exactly the number of checked bags in excess of the pooled free allowance (number of passengers x per-passenger allowance), with a per-passenger allowance of 1 bag in basic economy, 2 in economy and 3 in business.
rules.wiki_quote: If the booking user is a silver member, 1 free checked bag for each basic economy passenger, 2 free checked bag for each economy passenger, and 3 free checked bags for each business passenger.
rules.notes: See AIR-R020. Decision (Step 1 close-out): see AIR-R020 (exact equality, pooled allowance; reservation-level totals confirmed in the tool source).

rules.description: When the booking user is a gold member, the agent must set nonfree_baggages to exactly the number of checked bags in excess of the pooled free allowance (number of passengers x per-passenger allowance), with a per-passenger allowance of 2 bags in basic economy, 3 in economy and 3 in business.
rules.wiki_quote: If the booking user is a gold member, 2 free checked bag for each basic economy passenger, 3 free checked bag for each economy passenger, and 3 free checked bags for each business passenger.
rules.notes: See AIR-R020. Decision (Step 1 close-out): see AIR-R020 (exact equality, pooled allowance; reservation-level totals confirmed in the tool source).

rules.description: The agent must charge 50 dollars for each extra (non-free) checked bag.
rules.wiki_quote: Each extra baggage is 50 dollars.
rules.notes: The API adds 50 x nonfree_baggages to the price. The agent must quote and collect the same amount.

rules.description: The agent must ask the user whether they want to buy travel insurance before booking.
rules.wiki_quote: Travel insurance: the agent should ask if the user wants to buy the travel insurance
rules.notes: R27 had turned the obligation into a user option.

rules.description: The agent must charge travel insurance at 30 dollars per passenger when the user buys it.
rules.wiki_quote: which is 30 dollars per passenger
rules.notes: Split from compound R27. The coverage part (health or weather) is a fact and is used in AIR-R042.

rules.description: The agent must obtain the user id before modifying a reservation (flights, cabin, baggage, or passengers).
rules.wiki_quote: The agent must first obtain the user id and the reservation id.

rules.description: The agent must obtain the reservation id before modifying a reservation (flights, cabin, baggage, or passengers).
rules.wiki_quote: The agent must first obtain the user id and the reservation id.

rules.description: The agent must not change the flights of a basic economy reservation; for a basic economy reservation it may only change the cabin while keeping exactly the same flights (flight numbers and dates).
rules.wiki_quote: Change flights: Basic economy flights cannot be modified. … The API does not check these for the agent, so the agent must make sure the rules apply before calling the API! … Change cabin: all reservations, including basic economy, can change cabin without changing the flights.
rules.notes: Fixes R11, which banned all modification of basic economy reservations. 'Basic economy' means the reservation's current cabin. AMBIGUITY: whether flights can be changed after a cabin upgrade, in a separate later call. Literal reading: once upgraded, the reservation is no longer basic economy.

rules.description: When changing flights, the agent must keep the reservation's origin and destination unchanged.
rules.wiki_quote: Other reservations can be modified without changing the origin, destination, and trip type. … The API does not check these for the agent, so the agent must make sure the rules apply before calling the API!
rules.notes: Split from compound R12.

rules.description: When changing flights, the agent must keep the reservation's trip type (one way or round trip) unchanged.
rules.wiki_quote: Other reservations can be modified without changing the origin, destination, and trip type. … The API does not check these for the agent, so the agent must make sure the rules apply before calling the API! … Each reservation has an reservation id, user id, trip type (one way, round trip), flights, passengers, payment methods, created time, baggages, and travel insurance information.
rules.notes: Split from R12. This also blocks partial cancellation by dropping a leg of a round trip.

rules.description: When changing the cabin of a reservation, the agent must charge the user the price difference between the current and the new cabin class and must not waive it.
rules.wiki_quote: Cabin changes require the user to pay for the difference between their current cabin and the new cabin class.
rules.notes: The API computes the difference itself. Violations show up as promised free upgrades or offsets, e.g. via certificates. A downgrade yields a refund to the given payment method; the wiki says only 'pay for the difference'.

rules.description: The agent must apply a cabin change to all flights in the reservation and must not change the cabin of only some flight segments.
rules.wiki_quote: Cabin class must be the same across all the flights in the same reservation … changing cabin for just one flight segment is not possible.
rules.notes: Merges the redundant R16 and R17. The schema enforces this structurally (one cabin per call).

rules.description: The agent must not remove checked bags from a reservation: the new total number of checked bags must not be lower than the current total.
rules.wiki_quote: Change baggage and insurance: The user can add but not remove checked bags.
rules.notes: AMBIGUITY: the wiki does not say whether nonfree_baggages may decrease, e.g. by re-labelling bags as free. Literal check: total_baggages only.

rules.description: The agent must not add travel insurance to a reservation after it has been booked.
rules.wiki_quote: The user cannot add insurance after initial booking.
rules.notes: No τ-bench tool can add insurance to an existing reservation, so violations appear in messages: promising or claiming that insurance was added.

rules.description: The agent must not change the number of passengers in a reservation: an updated passenger list must have the same number of passengers as the current list.
rules.wiki_quote: Change passengers: The user can modify passengers but cannot modify the number of passengers.
rules.notes: The API also checks this.

rules.description: The agent must not transfer the user to a human agent for a request to change the number of passengers.
rules.wiki_quote: This is something that even a human agent cannot assist with.
rules.notes: Exception to AIR-R009: even a human agent cannot help, so the agent must deny instead.

rules.description: When changing flights, the agent must use exactly one payment method, which must be a gift card or a credit card from the user's profile (not a travel certificate).
rules.wiki_quote: Payment: If the flights are changed, the user needs to provide one gift card or credit card for payment or refund method.
rules.notes: R35 duplicates R20. Literal scope is 'if the flights are changed'. The same tool performs cabin changes, and the API rejects certificates for every update. Decision (Step 1 close-out): literal scope kept (applies only when the flights are changed). Tool source: update_reservation_flights rejects certificates for ANY call, flights changed or cabin only ('Error: certificate cannot be used to update reservation', update_reservation_flights.py:68-69), and takes a single payment_id. This rule is therefore API-enforced.

rules.description: When changing flights, the agent must ask the user which payment or refund method to use rather than choosing a method itself.
rules.wiki_quote: The agent should ask for the payment or refund method instead.
rules.notes: Restores the 'if the flights are changed' trigger. AMBIGUITY: the wiki does not say what 'instead' contrasts with. Read here as 'instead of choosing for the user'.

rules.description: The agent must obtain the user id before cancelling a reservation.
rules.wiki_quote: The agent must first obtain the user id, the reservation id, and the reason for cancellation (change of plan, airline cancelled flight, or other reasons)
rules.notes: R7 had lost the cancellation context.

rules.description: The agent must obtain the reservation id before cancelling a reservation.
rules.wiki_quote: The agent must first obtain the user id, the reservation id, and the reason for cancellation (change of plan, airline cancelled flight, or other reasons)

rules.description: The agent must obtain the user's reason for cancellation (change of plan, airline cancelled flight, or other reasons) before cancelling a reservation.
rules.wiki_quote: The agent must first obtain the user id, the reservation id, and the reason for cancellation (change of plan, airline cancelled flight, or other reasons)
rules.notes: Restores the enumeration of reasons.

rules.description: The agent must not cancel a basic economy or economy reservation unless it was created within the 24 hours before the current time, the airline cancelled a flight in the reservation, or travel insurance was bought and the cancellation reason is covered by it (health or weather).
rules.wiki_quote: All reservations can be cancelled within 24 hours of booking, or if the airline cancelled the flight. … Otherwise, basic economy or economy flights can be cancelled only if travel insurance is bought and the condition is met … and business flights can always be cancelled. … The rules are strict regardless of the membership status. … The API does not check these for the agent, so the agent must make sure the rules apply before calling the API! … and enables full refund if the user needs to cancel the flight given health or weather reasons. … The current time is 2024-05-15 15:00:00 EST.
rules.notes: This is one implication with three exceptions. Business reservations are not restricted by it (AIR-CAN-02d). Membership tier gives no exception (AIR-CAN-02e). AMBIGUITIES: (1) 'the condition is met' is read as the insurance condition of AIR-BOOK-05c (health or weather); (2) the 24-hour boundary is assumed inclusive, and created_at (no timezone) is assumed to be EST; (3) 'airline cancelled the flight' is read as any segment with flight status 'cancelled', a status the wiki never lists. The reason predicate (health/weather) is semantic, taken from the user's stated reason. Everything else is deterministic. Decision (Step 1 close-out): the hard-coded boundary date was removed. The current time is the config value policies/curated/airline_config.json:current_time (2024-05-15T15:00:00, EST); the validator checks it against clause AIR-CTX-01. Data note: no τ-bench v1 airline tool exposes a non-'available' flight status, so 'the airline cancelled a flight' cannot be verified from tool outputs (see policies/tau_bench/airline_data_notes.md).

rules.description: The agent must not cancel a reservation in which any flight segment has already been flown.
rules.wiki_quote: The agent can only cancel the whole trip that is not flown.
rules.notes: 'Whole trip' is structural: cancel_reservation always cancels the whole reservation. 'Flown' means segment status 'flying' or 'landed', or a flight date before 2024-05-15. AMBIGUITY: the wiki does not list 'landed'.

rules.description: If the user asks to cancel a reservation in which any flight segment has already been flown, the agent must transfer the user to a human agent.
rules.wiki_quote: If any of the segments are already used, the agent cannot help and transfer is needed.
rules.notes: Split from compound R43; R44 was a user-subject duplicate. Justifies a transfer under AIR-R008.

rules.description: The agent must not send a certificate to a user who is a regular member, has no travel insurance on the reservation, and flies basic economy or economy in it.
rules.wiki_quote: Do not compensate if the user is regular member and has no travel insurance and flies (basic) economy. … If the user is silver/gold member or has travel insurance or flies business, and complains about cancelled flights in a reservation, the agent can offer a certificate as a gesture … If the user is silver/gold member or has travel insurance or flies business, and complains about delayed flights in a reservation and wants to change or cancel the reservation, the agent can offer a certificate as a gesture
rules.notes: Fixes R37, which narrowed '(basic) economy' to basic economy. Eligibility is silver/gold OR insured OR business, as in AIR-COMP-01a and AIR-COMP-02a.

rules.description: The agent must not offer or send compensation unless the user has complained about the situation and explicitly asked for compensation.
rules.wiki_quote: Do not proactively offer these unless the user complains about the situation and explicitly asks for some compensation. … If the user is silver/gold member or has travel insurance or flies business, and complains about cancelled flights in a reservation, the agent can offer a certificate as a gesture … If the user is silver/gold member or has travel insurance or flies business, and complains about delayed flights in a reservation and wants to change or cancel the reservation, the agent can offer a certificate as a gesture
rules.notes: Restores the complaint trigger that R45 and R46 had weakened to 'experiences'.

rules.description: The agent must confirm the facts (that the flight in the user's reservation was actually cancelled or delayed, verified via tool lookups) before offering or sending a certificate.
rules.wiki_quote: after confirming the facts … after confirming the facts and changing or cancelling the reservation
rules.notes: Check: get_reservation_details, plus a flight-status lookup for the flight concerned, happen before send_certificate.

rules.description: For a complaint about a cancelled flight, the agent must set the certificate amount to exactly 100 dollars times the number of passengers in the reservation.
rules.wiki_quote: with the amount being $100 times the number of passengers. … If the user is silver/gold member or has travel insurance or flies business, and complains about cancelled flights in a reservation, the agent can offer a certificate as a gesture
rules.notes: Restores the dollar unit. Raw r45 had wrongly added 'wants to change or cancel' to this case.

rules.description: For a complaint about a delayed flight, the agent must send a certificate only if the user wanted to change or cancel the reservation and only after that change or cancellation has been completed.
rules.wiki_quote: If the user is silver/gold member or has travel insurance or flies business, and complains about delayed flights in a reservation and wants to change or cancel the reservation, the agent can offer a certificate as a gesture … after confirming the facts and changing or cancelling the reservation
rules.notes: Check: an update_reservation_flights or cancel_reservation call on that reservation occurs earlier in the trajectory.

rules.description: For a complaint about a delayed flight, the agent must set the certificate amount to exactly 50 dollars times the number of passengers in the reservation.
rules.wiki_quote: with the amount being $50 times the number of passengers. … If the user is silver/gold member or has travel insurance or flies business, and complains about delayed flights in a reservation and wants to change or cancel the reservation, the agent can offer a certificate as a gesture
